=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap
  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
  SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
  SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
  SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
  SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
  SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
  SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
  SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
  SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
  SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
  SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
  SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
  SPA-N-014: Category separation
  SPA-N-015: Title verification
  SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms

I reviewed all 16 items, including those tagged [STANDARD]. The Seller's "cleared by both sides" labels are the Seller's own characterisation. Nothing here shows the Buyer has agreed them, so I have treated every item as open. The positions below are drawn from the Seller's summary and Disclosure Letter, not the full SPA text, so clause references need checking against the draft. Figures marked as proposed opening positions are negotiating suggestions for the deal team to set.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** General Warranty Claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer should want:** Open at 100% of price (AUD 24m). A fallback in the range of 30–50% is a commercial call for the deal team.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** Four open disclosed issues already sit outside the general warranties, and a AUD 4.8m ceiling leaves little room to cover them.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis per claim; AUD 250k deductible basket (only the excess is recoverable).
- **Buyer should want:** A tipping basket (once exceeded, recovery from the first dollar). Proposed opening: de minimis around AUD 10k and basket around 0.5% of price (about AUD 120k).
- **Recommendation: Counter.** A deductible basket would leave up to AUD 250k of losses unrecoverable, and the de minimis would exclude smaller claims entirely.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion for general warranties, with the limitation applied to all Claims.
- **Buyer should want:** At least 36 months for general warranties. Tax claims run to the ATO amendment period plus a margin. Fundamental claims run for a longer period (see N-004).
- **Recommendation: Reject, counter at 36 months.** Eighteen months may expire before the open issues (Bluefen, Ironquay, privacy) crystallise.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties capped at 100% of price, outside the basket and de minimis, with a time limit of at least six years.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** The Buyer is paying AUD 24m for shares, and a AUD 4.8m cap on title would leave it exposed if title is defective.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Not addressed. The "limitations apply to all Claims of any nature" wording (cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5) would in practice catch fraud claims.
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out for fraud and wilful concealment from all caps, baskets, time limits, disclosure, non-reliance and knowledge provisions.
- **Recommendation: Add expressly.** The Seller's drafting would otherwise purport to limit fraud claims. Confirm with NSW counsel how non-reliance clauses interact with fraud and Australian Consumer Law misleading conduct protections.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (to 5pm, 22 September 2026), the Accounts and public registers, "without limiting any specific disclosure".
- **Buyer should want:** Only specific, fair disclosure against specific warranties, with documents identified. No general or deemed disclosure of the data room or public registers.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** General data-room disclosure would largely cancel the warranties, including for matters the Seller itself flags as open.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No Buyer claim for matters known or discoverable from the data room or public records (cl. 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** Deletion of the knowledge bar. Known issues should be dealt with through specific indemnities. An express clause should confirm that the Buyer's rights are unaffected by its knowledge, since the Australian position on this is not settled.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Under this wording, the Buyer would lose claims for the very issues the Disclosure Letter discloses.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl. 3/6.3). Disclosure states no final written consent and no evidence that conditions in cl. 11.3 are satisfied. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m (~30%) of FY26 revenue.
- **Buyer should want:** A final consent (or evidence that all conditions are satisfied) as a condition precedent, with a Seller obligation to procure it, a long-stop date and a walk-away right. If the Buyer waives it, a price adjustment or specific revenue-loss indemnity.
- **Recommendation: Reject the deemed-satisfaction wording.** About 30% of revenue depends on a consent that has not been given and whose conditions are unevidenced.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** AUD 3.2m facility to be released after Completion. Disclosure states the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included.
- **Buyer should want:** Repayment from the price at Completion under a payout letter, with discharge of security delivered at Completion and a PPSR search before Completion.
- **Recommendation: Reject the post-Completion release.** On a debt-free basis the Seller should clear this debt at Completion, not leave the Buyer holding secured debt.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** A "matter for the Seller". Disclosure states AUD 420k of conditional Completion bonuses are absent from the funds flow, and the on-cost position is unclear.
- **Buyer should want:** Treatment as a debt-like item deducted from price (or paid by the Seller), including employer on-costs such as payroll tax and superannuation. The funds flow to be corrected.
- **Recommendation: Counter, treat as debt-like.** Transaction-triggered bonuses are a Seller cost under a debt-free/cash-free structure, and the funds flow currently omits them.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment. Described as "adequate".
- **Buyer should want:** Payment of the AUD 180k open balance by the Seller before Completion (or a price deduction). A confirmatory assignment and evidence of payment as conditions. A specific indemnity covering IP title and third-party claims, outside the basket and de minimis, surviving until resolved.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Transfer of the Project Materials depends on payment that is not evidenced, so an indemnity limited to that payment misses the risk that the Company does not own the materials.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller:** "Preliminary", "not expected to be material". Disclosure does not characterise it as a breach and states no loss amount. About 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) may have been exposed to an unintended external address.
- **Buyer should want:** A forensic review before signing. An assessment of whether this is an eligible data breach under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Part IIIC and whether the Company is an APP entity (to be confirmed). A specific uncapped (or price-capped) indemnity for notification and regulatory costs, outside the basket. A holdback or escrow. A warranty of no other incidents.
- **Recommendation: Reject the "not material" characterisation.** Personal information about roughly 1,240 people has an unknown access status, and the statutory assessment timeline may already be running.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330k are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer should want:** The contracts, term lengths and termination rights. Confirmation that they are ordinary course. Pre-Completion commitments borne by the Seller or treated as debt-like. A covenant that no new renewals are made without Buyer consent.
- **Recommendation: Reject the label; require review.** The Disclosure Letter does not confirm the ordinary-course characterisation, and the timing and scope of three related renewals need checking.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** All limitations apply to all claims, so fundamental and general warranties are treated alike.
- **Buyer should want:** Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities (Riverlark, Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Bluefen) and fraud, each with its own cap, basket and time limit.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Merging the regimes would subject title and tax protection to the general cap and basket.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012 (Harbourglass Ventures holds 100%).
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification: a current ASIC extract, inspection of the register and share certificates, transfer documents, board and shareholder resolutions, and a PPSR search for encumbrances. The title warranty to be fundamental (N-004). Executed transfer documents and original certificates as completion deliverables.
- **Recommendation: Verify independently.** A register extract shows record title only and does not exclude prior transfers or encumbrances.

**SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime". No specific tax indemnity.
- **Buyer should want:** A pre-Completion tax indemnity, uncapped to price, with a time limit running to the ATO amendment period plus a margin. Tax warranties. IP ownership, non-infringement and sufficiency warranties treated as fundamental, with Ironquay addressed separately.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Tax and IP are typically the largest latent exposures and should not sit under general caps and time limits.

---

**Priority actions**
1. **Time-critical:** Privacy assessment for the export incident (N-012), Bluefen consent (N-008) and the Ironquay payment (N-011).
2. **Funds flow:** Correct for Riverlark payout (N-009) and bonuses with on-costs (N-010). Confirm payroll tax and superannuation treatment with tax advisers.
3. **Specialist input:** Privacy counsel (N-012), tax (N-010, N-016), and NSW counsel on the fraud carve-out and non-reliance (N-005).
4. **Document requests:** Full SPA text to confirm clause references; Sandbar contracts; Ironquay SOW3 evidence; PPSR and ASIC searches.
